⚔️ Saudis target Sanaa’s oil storage as Houthis urge civilians to evacuate areas around Aramco sites
🔊“The Yemeni Armed Forces are warning all employees and citizens located near any Saudi Aramco facility to evacuate the area and stay away from it, as these facilities are legitimate targets for our forces,” Ansar Allah-aligned military spokesman Yahya Saree said Tuesday.
Saree’s comments follow a similar warning from the Saudi-led coalition urging civilians to “evacuate the site of the Yemen Petroleum Company – the al-Sabaha Central Station” outside Sanaa. The warning was followed by an attack Tuesday afternoon.
Yemen Petroleum said the facility was not holding any fuel ready for distribution and sale at the time of the strike.
Before that attack, Saree warned that Riyadh would face a “harsh and painful response” if Yemen’s capital was struck, and that its international airport and main refinery would be targeted.
On Monday, Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman promised to ramp up the kingdom’s oil production and exports, notwithstanding Yemeni targeting of major facilities in Riyadh, Khurais, Yanbu, Abha, Najran and Jizan, and last month’s attack on the East-West [oil pipeline](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76084).
👉 The US Embassy in Riyadh issued a Level 3 travel advisory for Saudi Arabia Monday, urging Americans to “reconsider travel” “due to the risk of drone and missile targeting,” armed conflict, terrorism, exit bans “and local laws regarding social media activity” (it’s illegal to film and share info regarding missile and drone strikes).

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
💵 Big Tech wants 1M+ orbital data centers but fears they may be attacked
 
Facing public scrutiny over plans to build noisy, power-sucking, water-hogging AI host facilities in rural areas, tech CEOs are looking into the feasibility of putting them in space, where, theoretically, they’d have all [the space](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74895) and [solar power](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73521) they’d ever need.
Paying little mind to the risk of creating so much space junk it effectively seals humanity in on Earth forever (a phenomenon known as Kessler syndrome), Big Tech fears satellites may come under attack due to wars back on Earth, targeted by missiles, jamming, cyber or directed energy weapons. Russia, China, the US and India are known to possess or be working on such capabilities.
💬“Anything of value that you put up in space increases the potential payoff of attacking space infrastructure,” astropolitics researcher Bleddyn Bowen told Bloomberg. “We’d rather not have a shooting war in space because we’d all lose quite a lot.”
US Space Force assures it has “capabilities to protect and defend US space interests,” potentially including orbiting data centers, “if directed by appropriate decision-makers.”
Keppler launched the first elements of a dedicated space-based data center into low-Earth orbit in January with Axiom Space’s help. On October 2, SpaceX launched a Google data center test satellite.
Amazon’s Jeff Bezos and his private space company Blue Origin wants government permission to launch up to 50k such satellites. Elon Musk wants to put up to 1M in orbit.
Harvard astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell fears that in a conflict scenario, adversaries could not only target each other’s constellations, but deliberately create so much space junk that envisioned Sun-synchronous orbital trajectories become essentially “unusable.”

🪖🇺🇸 US military secretly operating in Lebanon, enjoys de facto control over its military, officer reveals
 
💬 “Officially, there is no declared US military base in Lebanon,” but “Americans are in fact present at Hamat Air Base…[and] at Rayak Air Base, where they oversee the drone operations facility, while a surveillance system covering the Masnaa area is located at the heart of Rayak,” a senior Lebanese Army officer told The Cradle.
Categorizing the US military and security presence and influence in the country as “exceptional,” the officer said there is a “very high level” of coordination, including “regular visits by CENTCOM officials.”
👉 The US decides what arms Lebanon gets, influences planning and training, and makes other decisions which raise “serious questions about the limits of Lebanese sovereignty,” the officer added, pointing out, for example, that when US military aircraft arrive, they are not subject to standard inspections.
The same is true for the US Embassy, a “huge, heavily fortified compound with extensive security and logistical infrastructure,” whose personnel have repeatedly provoked security incidents, from blocking roads, to stopping the mayor from approaching them, and even ordering Lebanese troops to withdraw.
‼️ The US ambassador has “a very broad scope for direct communication with the highest political, military, security and judicial levels,” behaving more like a viceroy than a diplomat.
Lebanon’s Army is very uncomfortable with political orders to cooperate with the IDF, considering the Israelis untrustworthy.
The Army is hesitant to implement [the government’s demands to disarm Hezbollah. ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75439)“There is a major difference between taking a political decision and having the ability to implement it on the ground.” The Army doesn’t want “to be pushed into a confrontation with a segment of the Lebanese population.”
Lebanon’s military also has no real ability to deter Israel from attacks, the officer lamented, saying[ the country lacks the air defenses, EW, artillery, missiles, anti-tank weapons, coastal defenses, independent C&C and intel systems](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76088) required.
